hook_candidates.spoken: A subagent has its own tools. What happens when it is not allowed to do something?
A subagent may do whatever Claude may do? Not if its file says otherwise.
The subagent could only read, so it found the typos but could not save them.
Without edit rights, the work fell back to the main session.
Two real runs: the same subagent, once with and once without Edit.

sources.title: Create custom subagents: each subagent runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions; frontmatter field tools: tools the subagent can use, as a comma-separated string such as Read, Grep, Bash; inherits every tool available to subagents if omitted

beats.spoken: A subagent has its own tools. What happens when it is not allowed to do something? Two real runs with a subagent called pruefer, which means checker.

The subagent is a file in the agents folder. Its header says which tools it may use: in run one only Read, in run two Read and Edit. According to the docs, every subagent has its own tool access and its own permissions.

data.quote: … with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions.
data.translation: Its own prompt, its own tools, its own permissions.

beats.spoken: The task: fix two typos in text.md, and have the subagent do it, not the main session.

Run one. Claude started pruefer in the background. The lines with the dotted bar come from the subagent. It read the file, but it was not allowed to write, so it could only report the typos. Claude then said it would fix them itself, and made the edit.
Run two, pruefer with Edit. This time the subagent read the file and changed it itself. Claude reported the result and added that it had not opened the file to confirm the edits.
Both runs ran twice, and the file was fixed at the end every time. The difference is who wrote it: in run one the main session, in run two the subagent. The limits in its file really applied.

data.headline: 2 runs, twice each
data.note: Own tools and permissions per subagent (per the docs).

beats.spoken: So give a subagent exactly the tools its job needs, and no more. Follow Promptwerk for more Claude workflows, step by step.

data.statement: Give each subagent only the tools it needs.
